title: Total-limit comparison and transposes of augmented tower arrows
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ a morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $u^*\dashv P=Ru_*$ for the canonical derived adjunction, with counit $\varepsilon$ and ordinary derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, use strict constant-$A$ towers on the small diagram sites [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], and let $\Delta$ be the constant-tower functor, $G=u^*$ termwise, $P^J=Ru_*^J$, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Normalize $\mathcal L_T\Delta\cong1$ on diagonal K-injective representatives and derive the adjunction $\Delta\dashv\lim$ from the ordinary module adjunction. Let
$$a_V:P\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}P^JV$$
be exactly the derived comparison from $u_*\lim=\lim u_*^J$ in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. For every $V\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_{\mathcal X})))$ and $M\in D_{\mathcal Y}$ the composite bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}P^JV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta M,P^JV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G\Delta M,V)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta u^*M,V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u^*M,\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V)$$
is the ordinary adjunction bijection after postcomposition with $a_V^{-1}$. Explicitly, for any tower objects $Z$ over $\mathcal Y$, $V$ over $\mathcal X$, arrow $b:GZ\to V$ with tower adjunct $b^\sharp:Z\to P^JV$, and $j:\Delta M\to Z$, the ordinary adjunct of the limit of $b\circ G(j)$ is
$$a_V^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(b^\sharp)\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(j):M\longrightarrow P\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V.$$
Here the source of the limit map is identified with $u^*M$ by $G\Delta=\Delta u^*$ and $\mathcal L\Delta=1$. This equality includes the actual counits and is natural in all displayed arguments. No perfectness, completeness or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Write $F=u^*$ and $U=u_*$ on ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves, and $U^J$ for levelwise direct image. The constant-ring identification and exactness of $F$ are supplied by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] gives the canonical module adjunction $F\dashv U$, with ordinary counit $\varepsilon^0$. Taking mates levelwise gives $F^J\dashv U^J$: naturality of $\varepsilon^0$ and of the ordinary unit makes these mates commute with every transition. The constant functors $\Delta_T$ and $F^J$ are exact because kernels and cokernels of towers are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Thus these functors descend termwise to the unbounded derived categories by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], with the literal representative identification $F^J\Delta_{\mathcal Y}=\Delta_{\mathcal X}F$.

proof.text: A map $B\to\lim_T W$ is precisely a compatible family $B\to W_n$, hence a map $\Delta_TB\to W$; this is the ordinary adjunction $\Delta_T\dashv\lim_T$. Also $1$ is terminal in $J$: a tower map $W\to\Delta_TB$ is uniquely given by $W_1\to B$, with component $W_n\to W_1\to B$. Therefore $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta_T$. Evaluation is exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows that $\Delta_TH$ is K-injective for every K-injective module complex $H$. The same lemma applied to the exact left adjoint $\Delta_T$ shows that $\lim_T$ preserves K-injective complexes. For $K=QH$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] now computes $\mathcal L_T\Delta_TK$ by $\lim_T\Delta_TH=H$: all projections are identities. Under this normalization the unit $K\to\mathcal L_T\Delta_TK$ of the derived constant/limit adjunction is the identity, since the ordinary unit is the cone of identity maps. This is the normalization required in the statement.

proof.text:
Use [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] to realize the two tower categories as module sheaves on small ringed sites; the indexing category and the original sites are small in the specified module universe. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], represent $V$ by a K-injective tower complex $H$. Since $F$ and $F^J$ are exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows that $U$ and $U^J$ preserve K-injectives. Together with step 2 this makes $\lim_{\mathcal X}H$, $U^JH$, $U\lim_{\mathcal X}H$ and $\lim_{\mathcal Y}U^JH$ K-injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] they compute all the derived functors appearing here. In particular the prescribed $a_V$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] is represented by the underived comparison
$$a_H^0:U\lim_{\mathcal X}H\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim_{\mathcal Y}U^JH.$$
It is the common-composite identification, satisfying $\pi_n^{UH}a_H^0=U(\pi_n^H)$; neither composite needs another resolution. This identifies the specified comparison, rather than choosing a possibly different isomorphism of right adjoints.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, first proof (common direct-image composite); derived.tex Tags 08BJ, 070K and 070Y

proof.text:
Choose any complex $B$ representing $M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every Hom set in the displayed chain is computed in the homotopy category using the targets in step 3: respectively $\lim_{\mathcal Y}U^JH$, $U^JH$, $H$, and $\lim_{\mathcal X}H$. The ordinary termwise adjunctions induce the homotopy adjunctions, with their actual units and counits, by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. For example the inverse to
$$\operatorname{Hom}_K(FB,\lim_{\mathcal X}H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(B,U\lim_{\mathcal X}H)$$
sends $c$ to $\varepsilon^0_{\lim H}\circ F(c)$. These homotopy bijections compute the canonical derived adjunctions: by [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived] the counit $\varepsilon'$ of the derived adjunction satisfies $G'(\beta_X)\circ\varepsilon'_{QX}=\alpha_{UX}\circ Q(\varepsilon^0_X)$, where the exact left functors are termwise with $\alpha$ the identity on representatives (step 1), and the right derived comparisons $\beta$ at the K-injective targets are the isomorphisms of step 3. Hence at each K-injective target the derived counit is the class of the ordinary counit, and the derived Hom bijection $g\mapsto\varepsilon'\circ G'(g)$ is the class of the formula above. The same construction applies to $\Delta_T\dashv\lim_T$, and identifies its unit with that of step 2. Thus we can check the requested identity on chain maps, without replacing any counit by an unspecified adjunction isomorphism.

proof.text:
Let $c:B\to\lim_{\mathcal Y}U^JH$ be a chain map. Through the first two inverse Hom bijections its image is the tower chain map $t:\Delta_{\mathcal X}FB\to H$ with
$$t_n=\varepsilon^0_{H_n}\circ F(\pi_n^{UH}\circ c).$$
The last bijection sends it to the unique chain map $d:FB\to\lim_{\mathcal X}H$ with $\pi_n^Hd=t_n$. On the other path, postcompose $c$ with $(a_H^0)^{-1}$ and take the ordinary adjunct; this gives $d'=\varepsilon^0_{\lim H}\circ F((a_H^0)^{-1}\circ c)$. Naturality of the ordinary counit and the defining projection equation of $a_H^0$ in step 3 give
$$\pi_n^Hd'=\varepsilon^0_{H_n}\circ F(U(\pi_n^H)\circ(a_H^0)^{-1}\circ c)=\varepsilon^0_{H_n}\circ F(\pi_n^{UH}\circ c)=t_n.$$
Uniqueness for the degreewise ordinary limit gives $d=d'$ as chain maps. The termwise adjunctions preserve homotopies, and every derived map into our targets is represented by a homotopy class by step 4. Localizing this equality therefore proves the asserted equality of Hom bijections for every $M,V$. The use of projections here is in the category of complexes; it does not assert that maps into a homotopy limit are detected by their projections in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, first proof; explicit agent calculation using the ordinary adjunction and degreewise limits

proof.text:
For the arrows in the statement put $k=b^\sharp\circ j:\Delta_{\mathcal Y}M\to P^JV$. Naturality in the source of the tower adjunction says that its transpose is $h=b\circ G(j):\Delta_{\mathcal X}FM\to V$; explicitly the transpose of $k$ is $\varepsilon^J_V\circ G(b^\sharp)\circ G(j)=b\circ G(j)$. Under $\Delta_{\mathcal Y}\dashv\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}$ the transpose of $k$ is $\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(k)\circ\eta_M=\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(b^\sharp)\circ\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(j)$ by the identity-unit normalization of step 2. Similarly the transpose of $h$ under $\Delta_{\mathcal X}\dashv\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}$ is $\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}(h)$ after identifying $\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}\Delta_{\mathcal X}FM=FM$. Apply step 5 to this $k$. The ordinary adjunct of that last limit map is exactly
$$a_V^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(b^\sharp)\circ\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(j).$$
This proves the explicit clause with its specified source identification.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; Tag 0940, section-derived-limits; agent application of steps 2 and 5 to the displayed arrows

proof.text: All the Hom bijections used above are natural, and the comparison $a$ is the fixed natural comparison of step 3. Consequently their equality is natural in $M,V$; composing with $j$ and the adjunction bijection gives naturality in the arrows and in $Z$ as well. The computation uses ordinary counits, which step 4 identifies with the specified derived counits, so it includes those actual counits. Only exact constant-coefficient pullback and K-injective resolutions on the small diagram sites were used. Neither the quotients $A/I^n$ nor any perfectness, completeness, boundedness, or exactness of countable products enters the argument. In particular it applies to zero objects, to $u=\mathrm{id}$, and to constant towers with the identity-unit normalization of step 2.
